component.name: git
component.title: Git
component.description: Run git operations, such as clone, commit, push and pull, on a local repository with JGit, and receive its commits, branches and tags.
component.label: file

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

healthCheckConsumerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckConsumerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all consumer based health checks from this component

healthCheckProducerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckProducerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all producer based health checks from this component. Notice: Camel has by default disabled all producer based health-checks. You can turn on producer checks globally by setting camel.health.producersEnabled=true.

CamelGitOperation.label: producer
CamelGitOperation.description: The operation that the producer performs, used only when the operation option is not set.

CamelGitFilename.label: producer
CamelGitFilename.description: The path of the file to stage (add) or to remove from the index and the working tree (remove), relative to the root of the working tree with / as separator. A directory stands for all the files below it, and file globs are not supported. Required by add and remove.

CamelGitCommitMessage.label: producer
CamelGitCommitMessage.description: The message of the new commit in commit and commitAll. Required by both.

CamelGitCommitUsername.label: producer
CamelGitCommitUsername.description: The name of the author and committer of the new commit in commit and commitAll. Used only together with CamelGitCommitEmail. Without both, JGit takes them from user.name and user.email of the git config.

CamelGitCommitEmail.label: producer
CamelGitCommitEmail.description: The email of the author and committer of the new commit in commit and commitAll. Used only together with CamelGitCommitUsername.

CamelGitCommitId.description: The commit id (the sha): of the commit consumed by the commit consumer, of the commit to cherry pick in a cherryPick operation, and of the new commit after a commit or commitAll operation

CamelGitAllowEmpty.label: producer
CamelGitAllowEmpty.description: Whether commit and commitAll create a commit when there is nothing to commit. Replaces the allowEmpty option.

CamelGitAuthorName.label: consumer
CamelGitAuthorName.description: The name of the author of the consumed commit.

CamelGitCommiterName.label: consumer
CamelGitCommiterName.description: The name of the committer of the consumed commit.

CamelGitCommitTime.label: consumer
CamelGitCommitTime.description: The commit time of the consumed commit, in seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z.

CamelGitBranchName.label: consumer
CamelGitBranchName.description: The full name of the consumed ref, such as refs/heads/main, refs/remotes/origin/main or refs/tags/v1. The branch and tag consumers set it and also put it in the body.

CamelGitBranchLeaf.label: consumer
CamelGitBranchLeaf.description: The full name of the ref that the consumed ref points to in the end, when it is a symbolic ref such as refs/remotes/origin/HEAD. For any other ref it is the same as CamelGitBranchName.

CamelGitBranchObjectId.label: consumer
CamelGitBranchObjectId.description: The id of the object that the consumed ref points to: a commit for a branch or a lightweight tag, a tag object for an annotated tag.

consumerOut.description: The full message of the commit with type=commit, the name of the ref, such as refs/heads/main or refs/tags/v1, with type=branch and tag. The commit id, author, committer and time, or the object id of the ref, are in headers

producerIn.description: Not used: the operations take their input from the options and headers, such as the file in CamelGitFilename and the message in CamelGitCommitMessage

producerOut.description: The result of JGit for the operation: the Status of status, the commits of log as a RevWalk read once, a List of Refs for showBranches and showTags, the PushResults of push, the Properties of the statistics of gc. The operations that change the repository, such as add and commit, keep the body. Without the operation option the operation is taken from the CamelGitOperation header

localPath.description: The path of the working tree of the local repository, the directory that holds the .git directory. The clone operation creates the repository there and fails if the directory exists, and init creates it there.

branchName.description: The name of the branch. The commit consumer receives the commits reachable from it, or the commits of all refs when it is not set or not found. For the producer it is the branch to create or delete, to check out (clone and checkout, which creates it when it does not exist) or to merge into targetBranchName (merge), and add, remove, commit, commitAll, status, log, push, pull, cherryPick and clean check out this existing branch first.

sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle.label: consumer
sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle.description: If the polling consumer did not poll any files, you can enable this option to send an empty message (no body) instead.

type.label: consumer
type.description: What the consumer receives: commit for each commit, tag for each tag, or branch for each local and remote-tracking branch. Required for the consumer. It receives all the existing items on its first poll and keeps the consumed ones in memory only, so after a restart it receives all of them again.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer,advanced

Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

pollStrategy.label: consumer,advanced
pollStrategy.description: A pluggable org.apache.camel.PollingConsumerPollingStrategy allowing you to provide your custom implementation to control error handling usually occurred during the poll operation before an Exchange have been created and being routed in Camel.

allowEmpty.label: producer
allowEmpty.description: Whether commit and commitAll create a commit when there is nothing to commit. If false, they fail with the EmptyCommitException of JGit instead, as git commit does without --allow-empty. The CamelGitAllowEmpty header replaces this option.

depth.label: producer
depth.description: The depth of a shallow clone in the clone operation, as the number of commits of history to fetch. For example, 1 fetches only the latest commit. The default 0 makes a full clone, and a negative value fails the clone.

operation.label: producer
operation.description: The operation that the producer performs. If not set, the producer takes it from the CamelGitOperation header.

remoteName.label: producer
remoteName.description: The name of the remote, such as origin, that pull, push and pushTag use and that remoteAdd adds. Required by these operations.

remotePath.label: producer
remotePath.description: The URL of the remote repository, such as https://github.com/apache/camel.git. The clone operation clones it, and remoteAdd adds it as the remote named remoteName.

tagName.label: producer
tagName.description: The name of the tag for createTag, which creates an annotated tag of HEAD, and for deleteTag and pushTag. For checkout, the tag that the new branchName branch starts from.

targetBranchName.label: producer
targetBranchName.description: The branch that the merge operation checks out and merges branchName into. If not set, merge uses init.defaultBranch of the user git config, or master when that is not set either.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

gitConfigFile.label: advanced
gitConfigFile.description: The git config file to read in place of the user git config (/.gitconfig), as a URI with the classpath:, file:, http: or https: scheme. When it is set, the system git config is not read.

backoffErrorThreshold.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffErrorThreshold.description: The number of subsequent error polls (failed due some error) that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

backoffIdleThreshold.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffIdleThreshold.description: The number of subsequent idle polls that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

backoffMultiplier.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffMultiplier.description: To let the scheduled polling consumer backoff if there has been a number of subsequent idles/errors in a row. The multiplier is then the number of polls that will be skipped before the next actual attempt is happening again. When this option is in use then backoffIdleThreshold and/or backoffErrorThreshold must also be configured.

greedy.label: consumer,scheduler
greedy.description: If greedy is enabled, then the ScheduledPollConsumer will run immediately again, if the previous run polled 1 or more messages.

healthCheckMaxPollDuration.label: consumer,scheduler
healthCheckMaxPollDuration.description: How long a poll may run before the health check of the consumer reports DOWN. The health check is otherwise based on the polls that are done, so it stays UP while a poll hangs, for example on a read without timeout from a connection that went silent. A poll includes routing the messages it polled, so set this above the longest poll you expect. The poll is not interrupted. The value is in millis (not affected by timeUnit). The default 0 turns this off.

initialDelay.label: consumer,scheduler
initialDelay.description: Milliseconds before the first poll starts.

repeatCount.label: consumer,scheduler
repeatCount.description: Specifies a maximum limit of number of fires. So if you set it to 1, the scheduler will only fire once. If you set it to 5, it will only fire five times. A value of zero or negative means fire forever.

runLoggingLevel.label: consumer,scheduler
runLoggingLevel.description: The consumer logs a start/complete log line when it polls. This option allows you to configure the logging level for that.

scheduledExecutorService.label: consumer,scheduler
scheduledExecutorService.description: Allows for configuring a custom/shared thread pool to use for the consumer. By default each consumer has its own single threaded thread pool.

scheduler.label: consumer,scheduler
scheduler.description: To use a cron scheduler from either camel-spring or camel-quartz component. Use value spring or quartz for built in scheduler

schedulerProperties.label: consumer,scheduler
schedulerProperties.description: To configure additional properties when using a custom scheduler or any of the Quartz, Spring based scheduler. This is a multi-value option with prefix: scheduler.

startScheduler.label: consumer,scheduler
startScheduler.description: Whether the scheduler should be auto started.

timeUnit.label: consumer,scheduler
timeUnit.description: Time unit for initialDelay and delay options.

useFixedDelay.label: consumer,scheduler
useFixedDelay.description: Controls if fixed delay or fixed rate is used. See ScheduledExecutorService in JDK for details.

password.label: producer,security
password.description: The password, or an access token, to authenticate with the remote repository in clone, pull, push and pushTag. Used only when username is set too.

username.label: producer,security
username.description: The user name to authenticate with the remote repository in clone, pull, push and pushTag. Used only when password is set too.
